weeks.rationale: Re-anchor week, 14 weeks to Hyrox #2 and the opening week of the aggressive volume ramp (base_weekly_km raised 53 -> 62, band now 55.8-68.2 km). Tuesday's threshold session is replaced by a 30-minute field time trial: the zones every prescription depends on were measured on 2026-06-19 and the whole macrocycle is about to be calibrated to them, so testing at this block boundary while still fresh off the race taper is worth more than one more threshold workout. Volume steps to 62.5 km, mid-band rather than top, because the test needs fresh legs and this is already a large jump from the post-race week. Everything after Tuesday should be re-targeted to whatever the TT returns.
weeks.methodology: Testing before prescribing: a lab-anchored pace is only as good as its age, and a threshold that has improved silently makes every subsequent session too easy, which is the failure mode a flat-band plan hides best. The 30-minute TT is the standard field proxy for LT2 - average pace across the effort approximates threshold pace and average HR over the final twenty minutes approximates LTHR - and it doubles as a genuine threshold stimulus, so nothing is lost from the week's training even if the numbers come back unchanged. Around it the week stays polarized, with one hard day, one moderate station day, and the rest genuinely easy. The new gym-daily and home-treadmill availability is used to place gym work in the morning and running in the afternoon rather than to lengthen single runs, which is what keeps a 22% volume jump absorbable.

sessions.title: Upper Pull, arms-only (AM) + Easy Aerobic (PM)
sessions.prescription: AM (gym, ~40 min) STRICTLY UPPER BODY - time trial tomorrow, so nothing loads the legs or lower back: weighted pull-up 4x5 @ bodyweight +5 kg; overhead press 4x4 @ 60 kg; chest-supported single-arm DB row 3x8 per side @ 32 kg; dumbbell bench press 3x6 @ 2x32 kg; bent-over DB rear-delt raise 3x12 @ 8-10 kg. Free weights only. Leave 2-3 reps in reserve on every set - no grinding, no failure, no movements you have not done before. Deliberately NO barbell bent-over row and NO loaded carries this week (both tax the posterior chain). PM (home treadmill or outdoors): 56 min genuinely easy, HR <=138 bpm, conversational.

steps.target: RPE 8, ~2 RIR - full hang each rep
chest supported on a bench - no torso swing
RPE 7, light and strict - log the load

sessions.purpose: Aerobic volume with zero residual fatigue carried into the time trial.
sessions.why: A full upper session is worth the gym trip and the legs are idle before tomorrow's trial anyway, so this is free training time rather than added cost. What is controlled is not the length but the proximity to failure and the choice of movements: every exercise here is arms-and-torso only, so nothing touches the muscles that run, and the barbell row and farmers carry that appear in later weeks are cut because both load the posterior chain. Everything stops 2-3 reps short so tomorrow's heart rate - half the measurement, and the baseline every future test is compared against - is not carrying yesterday's fatigue. Pull-dominant because vertical pulling is the weakest quality on file and the sled pull and ski erg both demand it.

sessions.title: 30-min Threshold TT (BENCHMARK) + Heavy Lower (double)
sessions.prescription: AM (no gym) BENCHMARK - 30-MIN TIME TRIAL: 20 min easy warmup with 3x1 min builds (~3.5 km) -> 30 min all-out time trial, even effort, run as a race (~6.8 km). Press lap at 10 min: average HR over the FINAL 20 MIN = your LTHR, average pace over the full 30 min = your threshold pace. TREADMILL at 1% incline, no handrails, FAN ON YOU (indoor heat stress inflates HR and HR is half the measurement). Self-paced steps: start 13.5 km/h; at 10 min +0.5 if RPE<=7; at 20 min +0.5 if still holding form; empty it over the last 5. Read TOTAL DISTANCE off the console at 30:00 -> threshold pace = 30 / distance. Note which treadmill - every future re-test must use the same one. -> 15 min easy cooldown (~2.6 km). PM (gym, maintenance only): back squat 3x3 @ 100 kg, trap-bar deadlift 2x3 @ 130 kg. No plyometrics, no hip thrust. LOG THE TT RESULT - the block's remaining zones depend on it.

steps.target: all-out but EVEN - start 13.5 km/h, step +0.5 at 10 and 20 min
avg HR of final 20 min = LTHR; avg pace of full 30 min = threshold pace

sessions.purpose: Re-anchor LTHR and threshold pace with a field test, while delivering a full threshold stimulus.

A 30-min TT costs nothing in training terms because a maximal 30-minute effort IS a threshold session, so this is a free measurement rather than a week spent testing. Lifting is cut to two top-end movements rather than the usual three: the day already contains a maximal effort, and the point of the PM session is to hold strength, not add to it.

sessions.prescription: 66 min easy (HR <=142 bpm, ~5:30-5:50/km) -> 6x3 min @ race pace (~4:50/km) with 2 min easy jog between -> 5 min easy cooldown.
sessions.purpose: Long aerobic run finished with race-pace running on pre-fatigued legs.
sessions.why: Long-run duration builds LT2 from below while Tuesday's threshold builds it from above. The race-pace finish is added because it is the cheapest specific work in the week - a few minutes at goal pace on already-fatigued legs - and running the long run flat was leaving that adaptation unclaimed for no reason. Still an endurance run with a finish, not a workout, so it costs no extra recovery day.

sessions.title: Rest
sessions.prescription: Full rest. Review the block before the next one is generated: did 67 km land, and what did the TT change?
sessions.purpose: Close the block with full recovery and a review point.
sessions.why: The last day of a four-week block is the natural place to be genuinely empty, since the next block should start from absorbed work rather than accumulated fatigue. It is also the review gate: whether this week felt sustainable decides if base_weekly_km climbs again in September or holds at 62.
